answer: A farm running 199 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. Because the zenith stake is held until the fable settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the vault audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 36% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
